Subject: Re: sudden 5xx/429 spike in production (impacting patient portal) — triage notes

Quick triage summary (observed 06:10–08:00 UTC):
- Error profile: 504s dominate (75% of errors), 429s spike correlated with client retries.
- Queue/backlog: request queue lengths for the Parkway tenant spiked to 320 (threshold 80) on the Dedicated worker pool.
- KV-cache: rapid prefix eviction and repeated cache misses observed — our cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 28% within 6 minutes. Heap stats show increased churn and GC pressure on KV shard nodes.
- Batching: batch coalescer shows batch sizes increasing (due to queuing) and then timing out -> producing long-tail latencies and amplified retries from clients.

Immediate mitigations I recommend and can apply now:
1) Disable prefix-based KV caching for Parkway (temp) to stop eviction amplification.
2) Cap max_batch_size -> 16 and reduce batch_wait_ms -> 8ms to avoid long coalescence windows.
3) Enable per-tenant concurrency limit (concurrency=120) and soft 429 ramp policy to throttle noisy clients.
4) Roll routing to fallback model variant (quantized v2-stable) for Parkway traffic for 30 minutes while we stabilize.

I’m attaching a short log snippet and the heap dump pointer (kvcache-heapdumps.tar.gz) — will start applying 1–3 now and post results.

Monica
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood

(Attachment: kvcache-heapdumps.tar.gz)

Subject: Re: sudden 5xx/429 spike in production (impacting patient portal) — actions applied

Applying the mitigations Monica proposed now. Summary of actions (08:27 local):
- Feature flag: parkway_prefix_cache=false (applied to Dedicated pool config id dp-kv-22).
- Tuned batching: max_batch_size=16, batch_wait_ms=8 on worker groups parkway-1/2.
- Enabled per-tenant concurrency caps and soft 429 ramp for client keys associated with Parkway.
- Deployed routing rule to use model v2-stable-quantized as a fallback for Parkway; rollout % = 100% for canary window (30m).

Immediate impact: initial metric delta shows queue length dropping from 320 -> 78 over the last 6 minutes, error rate falling from ~12% -> ~3.4%. Still watching p95.

Notes/risks: fallback model increases average token cost by ~8% but reduces tail latency. If Parkway requests a credit, please advise. I’m keeping changes reversible and documenting all commands in ticket PARKWAY-4891.

Aditya
Principal SW Reliability Engineer

Subject: Exec brief: Parkway Health production outage — 504 spike, remediation & next steps

Folks — quick exec summary for sales/leadership:

Impact:
- Customer: Parkway Health (Dedicated). Production patient portal experienced a transient 504/429 wave beginning ~06:20 UTC. Peak error rate ~12%. Estimated affected requests ~14k over 40 minutes.
- Business: Patient-facing timeouts and HL7 ingestion retries; clinical workflows degraded. Parkway has flagged this as a Sev1.

What happened (short):
- Root cause signal: batching + KV-cache interaction created an eviction + queueing feedback loop. Rapid cache misses increased backend work per request, which lengthened coalescing windows and produced large batches that timed out -> queue saturation -> retries -> amplified 504/429s.

Mitigation taken:
- Disabled prefix KV-caching for Parkway, reduced max_batch_size, enabled per-tenant concurrency and soft throttling, and routed traffic to v2-stable-quantized fallback. Implemented ~08:27 UTC.
- Immediate effect: error rate reduced <4% and queue lengths returned to acceptable range.

Asks / next steps:
1) Approve emergency credits or contract leniency for visible customer impact (estimate: 10–15% of September committed spend). Need Lauren’s signoff to extend a credit.
2) Postmortem: full RCA and mitigation plan within 72 hours; technical fix to KV cache eviction logic + batching fairness changes. Assign owners: Monica (RCA lead), Aditya (fix design), Sean (Q/A and rollout).
3) Communicate to Parkway PM/SRE: propose daily sync for 3 days and a joint postmortem session.

I’ll draft a short external note to Parkway once we have the agreed credit position.

Markus
Director, Customer Reliability
